expected_effect: Lower val_bpb by 0.001 to 0.004 at a matched step count (~2071 steps, within 3% of the trn21 control 1.005734 / 2071). Direction predeclared: negative delta. A result within +/-0.0005 at matched steps is a null; a positive delta of >0.001 falsifies the noise-annealing hypothesis (i.e. the tables need the full LR through the tail to keep absorbing new n-grams).
hypothesis: The hashed n-gram value-embedding tables (the single largest measured win in the repo, 4 tables of 1048576x128 on layers 1 and -1, RMSProp-trained) are the only large parameter family whose learning rate is held FLAT through the 75%-of-budget LR warmdown (NGRAM_VE_FLAT_LR default True). Every other tensor's step size decays to FINAL_LR_FRAC=0.05 of peak, which is what lets the final ~1500 cooldown steps converge instead of bounce; the tables never get that annealing, so their entries carry full-amplitude RMSProp noise into the final checkpoint. Letting the tables follow the same cooldown multiplier (--no-ngram-ve-flat-lr) should reduce end-of-run table noise and lower val_bpb at an unchanged step count, because it is a pure per-step schedule change that adds no ops, tensors, or parameters.
single_causal_change: Pass --no-ngram-ve-flat-lr only (NGRAM_VE_FLAT_LR False: the n-gram VE table learning rate follows the run's LR warmdown instead of being held flat). Every other option stays at the 9a4caa7b defaults used by the two pinned controls: identical launch shape (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2, torchrun --nproc_per_node=4, --num-steps 5000 --max-train-seconds 1800 --seed 42, NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--optlevel=1'). No precision flag, no kernel flag, no optimizer switch, no architecture switch, no --ngram-ve-lr/--ngram-ve-opt/--ngram-ve-beta2 change, no data/evaluator change.
